questions.question: Which objects can you use in a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) script?
questions.explanation: In a Scheduled Job script, you have access to GlideSystem (gs) and GlideRecord. The current object is not available because Scheduled Jobs run in the background without a specific record context. GlideUser is a client-side API and is not available in server-side scheduled scripts.

questions.question: Which script debugger filter helps filter debugging searches to quickly narrow down problems?
questions.explanation: The Script Tracer is the feature within the ServiceNow Script Debugger that lets developers trace server-side script execution. You specify which scripts, events, and log messages to monitor, effectively filtering debug output to focus on specific code and quickly narrow down problems. Why others are wrong: B) 'Session tracer' is not the correct term for this feature. C) 'Script search' is for finding code locations, not tracing execution. D) 'Script filter' describes the function but is not the official feature name.

questions.question: When a ServiceNow instance requests information from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service:
questions.explanation: When ServiceNow requests information from an external web service, it is acting as the Consumer. The external system hosting and serving the data is the Provider. 'Publisher' and 'Specialist' are not standard web service roles in this context.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the fastest way to create and configure a Record Producer?
options: Create a Catalog Category, open the category, and select the Add New Record Producer button
Use the Record Producer module then add and configure all variables manually
Open the table in the Table records and select the Add to Service Catalog Related Link
Open the table's form, right-click on the form header, and select the Create Record Producer menu item
questions.explanation: The fastest way is to open the table and select 'Add to Service Catalog' related link. This not only creates the Record Producer but also automatically generates variables for the table's fields, saving significant manual effort. Other methods require more steps or manual variable configuration.

questions.question: Which of the following methods are useful in Access Control scripts?
questions.explanation: In ACL scripts (server-side), gs.hasRole() checks if the current user has a specific role, and current.isNewRecord() checks if the record is new. g_user is a client-side object (not available in ACLs), and current.isNew() is not a valid method — the correct method is isNewRecord().

questions.question: Which one of the following client-side scripts apply to Record Producers?
options: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies
UI Scripts and Record Producer Scripts
questions.explanation: Record Producers use Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies for client-side scripting. Standard Client Scripts and UI Policies apply to regular forms, not to Service Catalog items or Record Producers.

questions.question: When configuring an Access Control which has no condition or script, which one of the following statements is NOT true?
options: table.* will grant access to every field in a record
table.None will grant access to every record on the table
table.field will grant access to a specific field in a record
table.id will grant access to a specific record on the table
questions.explanation: table.id is NOT a valid ACL configuration — it does not grant access to a specific record. The correct ACL types are: table.* (all fields), table.None (record-level access), and table.field (specific field access). Record-level restrictions require conditions or scripts, not a 'table.id' rule.

questions.question: How must Application Access be configured to prevent all other private application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables?
options: You must create Access Controls to prevent all other application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables rather than using Application Access
Set the Accessible from field value to All application scopes and de-select the Can create option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only and de-select the Allow access to this table via web services option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only
questions.explanation: To prevent all other scopes from creating records, simply set Accessible from to 'This application scope only'. This restricts all cross-scope operations (create, read, update, delete) to the owning application. No additional ACLs or de-selections are needed.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a method used for logging messages in a server-side script for a privately-scoped application?
questions.explanation: gs.log() is NOT available in privately-scoped applications. The valid logging methods for scoped apps are gs.error(), gs.warn(), gs.debug(), and gs.info(). gs.log() is only available in the global scope.

questions.question: If the Create module field is selected when creating a table, what is the new module's default behavior?
options: Open an empty form so new records can be created
Open a link to a wiki article with instructions on how to customize the behavior of the new module
Display an empty homepage for the application
Display a list of all records from the table
questions.explanation: When you select 'Create module' during table creation, the new module's default behavior is to display a list of all records from that table. Clicking the module in the Application Navigator opens the list view.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository?
questions.explanation: To link to Git, you need the repository URL, username, and password/token for authentication. The Application name is used for identification within ServiceNow Studio but is NOT part of the Git linking credentials.

questions.question: Which Report Type(s) can be created by right-clicking on a column header in a table's list?
options: Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Histogram, and Line
Bar Chart, Pie Chart, and Histogram
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a column header in a list view allows you to create Bar Chart and Pie Chart reports. Histograms and Line charts are not available from the column context menu.

questions.question: What is a Module?
options: The functionality within an application menu such as opening a page in the content frame or a separate tab or window
A group of menus, or pages, providing related information and functionality to end-users
A way of helping users quickly access information and services by filtering the items in the Application Navigator
A web-based way of providing software to end-users
questions.explanation: A Module is the functional item within an application menu that performs a specific action — such as opening a list, displaying a form, or launching a page. Option B describes an Application Menu, C describes the Navigator filter, and D describes SaaS.

questions.question: It is best practice to define the business requirements and the process(es) an application will manage as part of the application development plan. What are some of the considerations to document as part of the business process?
options: Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, project schedule, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and database capacity
Business problem, users/stakeholders, available licenses, and database capacity
questions.explanation: The key considerations for documenting business processes are: business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps. Project schedule, database capacity, and available licenses are technical/operational concerns, not core business process documentation items.

questions.question: Which of the following statements does NOT apply when extending an existing table?
options: The parent table's Access Controls are evaluated when determining access to the new table's records and fields
The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table
The new table inherits all of the fields from the parent table
You must script and configure all required behaviors
questions.explanation: When extending a table, the child table inherits the parent's fields, functionality, and access controls. You do NOT need to script and configure all required behaviors from scratch — that's the whole benefit of table extension.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a purpose of application scoping?
options: Provide a relationship between application artifacts
Provide a way of tracking the user who developed an application
Provide a namespace (prefix and scope name) to prevent cross application name collisions
Provide controls for how scripts from another scope can alter tables in a scoped application
questions.explanation: Tracking the user who developed an application is NOT a purpose of application scoping. Scoping provides: artifact relationships (A), namespaces to prevent naming conflicts (C), and cross-scope access controls (D). Developer tracking is handled by metadata/version history, not scoping.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true regarding Application Scope?
options: All applications are automatically part of the Global scope
Applications downloaded from 3rd party ServiceNow application developers cannot have naming conflicts
Any developer can edit any application
Developers can choose the custom portion of a scope's namespace, which is prefixed with 'x_'
questions.explanation: Application Scope ensures isolation between applications, so third-party apps cannot have naming conflicts thanks to unique namespaces. A is wrong (scoped apps are NOT in Global scope), C is wrong (scope enforces boundaries), and D is wrong (the 'x_' prefix is auto-generated, not manually chosen).

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement about Delegated Development in ServiceNow.
options: Administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications.
Administrators can specify which application file types the developer can access.
Administrators can grant the developer access to script fields.
Administrators can grant the developer access to security records.
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is A. Delegated Development is designed for scoped applications only, not global applications. Administrators can specify file types (B), grant script access (C), and grant security record access (D) within the delegated scope.

questions.question: One of the uses of the ServiceNow REST API Explorer is:
options: Practice using REST to interact with public data providers
Find resources on the web for learning about REST
Convert SOAP Message functions to REST methods
Create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow
questions.explanation: The REST API Explorer lets developers test and generate sample code (cURL, Python, JavaScript) for sending REST requests to ServiceNow APIs. It does not interact with public providers (A), teach REST (B), or convert SOAP to REST (C).

questions.question: In a Business Rule, which one of the following returns true if the currently logged in user has the admin role?
questions.explanation: Business Rules are server-side, so you must use gs.hasRole('admin'). g_form is client-side only (A, C are invalid in Business Rules). gs.hasRoleExactly() does not exist in the GlideSystem API (D is invalid).

questions.question: From the list below, identify one reason an application might NOT be a good fit with ServiceNow. The application:
options: Requires 'as-is' use of low-level programming libraries
Uses forms extensively to interact with data
questions.explanation: ServiceNow does NOT support low-level programming libraries — it uses its own APIs with a low-code approach. Workflow (A), reporting (C), and form-based data interaction (D) are all core strengths of the ServiceNow platform.

questions.question: When configuring a REST Message, the Endpoint is:
options: The commands to the REST script to stop execution
The URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified
Information about the format of the returned data
The response from the provider indicating there is no data to send back
questions.explanation: The Endpoint is the URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) that specifies the target location where the REST call is sent. It is not about stopping execution (A), data format (C), or empty responses (D).

questions.question: When evaluating Access Controls, ServiceNow searches and evaluates:
options: Only for matches on the current table
Only for matches on the current field
From the most specific match to the most generic match
From the most generic match to the most specific match
questions.explanation: ServiceNow evaluates ACLs from most specific to most generic: field-level ACLs are checked first, then table-level ACLs. This ensures fine-grained security is applied before broader rules. D is the reverse of the actual order; A and B are incomplete.

questions.question: When configuring a module, what does the Override application menu roles configuration option do?
options: Users with the module role but without access to the application menu access the module
Self-Service users can access the module even though they do not have roles
Admin is given access to the module even if Access Controls would ordinarily prevent access
Users with access to the application menu can see the module even if they don't have the module role
questions.explanation: The Override application menu roles option allows users who have the module-specific role to access the module directly, even if they don't have access to the parent application menu. It does not bypass ACLs (C) or grant access to users without roles (B).

questions.question: Which platform feature can be used to determine the relationships between fields in an Import Set table to fields in an existing ServiceNow table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map determines the relationships (field mappings) between an Import Set table and a target ServiceNow table. Data Sources define where data comes from, but Transform Maps define how fields map between source and target.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true for a Script Include with a Protection Policy value of Protected?
options: Any user with the protected_edit role can see and edit the Script Include
The Protection policy option can only be enabled by a user with the admin role
The Protection Policy is applied only if the glide.app.apply_protection system property value is true
The Protection Policy is applied only if the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store
questions.explanation: The Protection Policy on a Script Include is enforced only when the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow Store. In the development instance, the policy is not applied. The 'Read-only' option allows others to view but not edit the script include.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true for GlideUser (g_user) methods?
options: Can be used in Client Scripts and UI Policies only
Can be used in Business Rules only
Can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions
Can be used in Business Rules, and Script Includes
questions.explanation: g_user is a client-side object available in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions (when the 'Client' checkbox is enabled). It is NOT available in server-side scripts like Business Rules or Script Includes.

questions.question: Which roles grant access to source control repository operations such as importing applications from source control, or linking an application to source control? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The roles required for source control operations are admin and source_control. There is no source_control_admin or git_admin role in ServiceNow's source control framework.

questions.question: When configuring the content of a Notification Email script, which syntax should be used to reference the parameters of an event triggering the Notification?
questions.explanation: In Notification Email Scripts, the event object is available for notifications triggered by events. Use event.parm1 and event.parm2 to reference the event's parameters. The other options use template syntax for different purposes.

questions.question: Which method call returns true only if the currently logged in user has the catalog_admin role and in no other case?
questions.explanation: g_user.hasRoleExactly('catalog_admin') returns true only if the user has exactly that role. g_user.hasRole() would also return true for admin users (who inherit all roles). hasRoleOnly() and hasRoleFromList() are not valid ServiceNow API methods.

questions.question: There is a basic strategy when creating a Utils Script Include. Identify the step that does not belong.
options: Create a prototype object from the new class
questions.explanation: A Utils Script Include is designed for reusable utility functions that are NOT tied to a specific table. Identifying a table is not part of the strategy. The correct steps are: script the functions (B), create a class (C), and create a prototype object (D).

This is a self-invoking function (also called an IIFE — Immediately Invoked Function Expression). It defines a function and immediately executes it by wrapping it in parentheses and calling it with arguments. It is not a constructor (A), and while technically anonymous (C), the primary characteristic is self-invocation.

questions.question: When working in the Form Designer, configuring the label of a field in a child table changes the label on which table(s)?
questions.explanation: When you change a field label in Form Designer on a child table, the label change applies to all tables that share that field (parent and other child tables). This is because the field's label is defined at the dictionary level, not per-table.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true?
options: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts
The execution order for a UI Policy's Scripts and Actions is determined at runtime
A UI Policy's Scripts execute before the UI Policy's Actions
A UI Policy's Actions and Scripts execute at the same time
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow, UI Policy Actions execute first (setting fields to mandatory, read-only, or visible), and then UI Policy Scripts execute afterward. This allows scripts to build on or override the behavior defined by the Actions.

questions.question: Modules must have a Link type. Which one of the following is a list of Link types?
options: List of Records, Separator, Catalog Type, Roles
Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page
List of Records, Content Page, Order, URL (from arguments:)
Assessment, List of Records, Content Page, Roles
questions.explanation: Valid module Link types include Assessment, List of Records, Separator, and Timeline Page. 'Catalog Type', 'Roles', and 'Order' are NOT valid module link types.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true for a table with the 'Allow configuration' Application Access option selected?
options: Only the in scope application's scripts can create Business Rules for the table
Any user with the application's user role can modify the application's scripts
Out of scope applications can create Business Rules for the table
Out of scope applications can add new tables to the scoped application
questions.explanation: The Allow Configuration option permits out-of-scope applications to create application files for the table, including Business Rules, Client Scripts, new fields (dictionary entries), and UI Actions. It does NOT allow adding new tables to the scoped application (D).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT supported by Flow Designer?
options: Call a subflow from a flow
Run a flow from a MetricBase Trigger
questions.explanation: Flow Designer does NOT support testing with rollback — that feature exists in the legacy Workflow Editor. Flow Designer does support subflows (A), delegated development (C), and MetricBase triggers (D).

questions.question: Which of the following are true for reports in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)
options: Any user can see any report shared with them.
Can be a graphical representation of data.
All users can generate reports on any table.
Can be run on demand by authorized users.
Can be scheduled to be run and distributed by email.
questions.explanation: Reports can be graphical (B), run on demand by authorized users (D), and scheduled for email distribution (E). A is wrong because users must have rights to view the report data. C is wrong because Access Controls restrict report generation on certain tables.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a UI Action type?
questions.explanation: Form choice is NOT a valid UI Action type. The valid types are: Form button, Form link, Form context menu, List choice, List banner button, and List bottom button.

questions.question: In an Email Notification, which one of the following is NOT true for the Weight field?
options: Only Notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipients are sent
A Weight value of zero means that no email should be sent
The Weight value defaults to zero
A Weight value of zero means the Notification is always sent when the Notification's When to send criteria is met
questions.explanation: A weight of zero does NOT mean no email is sent. It means the notification always sends when criteria are met (D is true). Only non-zero weighted notifications compete, with the highest weight winning (A is true). The default weight is zero (C is true).

questions.question: Which of the following objects does a Display Business Rule NOT have access to?
questions.explanation: Display Business Rules run before a record form is loaded for viewing. At this stage, the previous object is not available (it only exists during update operations). Display rules DO have access to current, GlideSystem (gs), and g_scratchpad — in fact, populating g_scratchpad is the primary purpose of Display Business Rules.

questions.question: When creating new application files in a scoped application, cross scope access is turned on by default in which of the following?
questions.explanation: When creating a new custom table in a scoped application, cross-scope read access is enabled by default. Other application scopes can read from the table without explicit configuration. Script Includes, REST Messages, and Workflows default to 'This application scope only'.

questions.question: Which Application Access configuration field(s) are NOT available if the Can read configuration field is NOT selected?
options: All access to this table via web services
Can create, Can update, and Can delete
Can read does not affect the availability of other Application Access fields
questions.explanation: If Can read is NOT selected, then Can create, Can update, and Can delete are also unavailable. Read access is the foundation — without it, other CRUD operations cannot be granted to other scopes.

questions.question: Which source control operation is available from BOTH Studio and the Git Repository?
questions.explanation: Create Branch is available from both Studio and the Git Repository. Other operations like Apply Remote Changes, Stash Local Changes, and Edit Repository Configurations are available in only one of the two interfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following methods prints a message on a blue background to the top of the current form by default?
questions.explanation: g_form.addInfoMessage() displays a blue informational banner at the top of the form. g_form.addInfoMsg() is not a valid method. showFieldMessage() and showFieldMsg() display messages next to specific fields, not at the form top.

questions.question: A scoped application containing Flow Designer content dedicated to a particular application is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A Spoke is a scoped application containing Flow Designer content dedicated to a particular application or record type. Activating a spoke adds application-specific core actions to Flow Designer.

questions.question: What syntax is used in a Record Producer script to access values from Record Producer form fields?
questions.explanation: In Record Producer scripts, use producer.variablename to access form input values. The current object refers to the target record being created — you use it to SET values (e.g., current.short_description = producer.short_desc), not to read Record Producer inputs.

questions.question: How many application menus can an application have?
options: 3, one for an application's user modules, one for an application's administrator modules, and one for the ServiceNow administrator's modules
As many as the application design requires
2, one for an application's user modules and one for an application's administrator modules
1, which is used for all application modules
questions.explanation: There is no fixed limit on the number of application menus. An application can have as many menus as the design requires to organize modules by functionality, roles, or user experience needs.

questions.question: The source control operation used to store local changes on an instance for later application is called a(n) ______.
questions.explanation: The Stash operation in ServiceNow source control stores local changes on an instance for later application, similar to git stash. It temporarily saves your work without committing it.

questions.question: Which one of the following is part of the client-side scripting API?
questions.explanation: The GlideUser object (g_user) is part of the client-side API, available in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions. current and previous are server-side (Business Rules), gs is server-side (GlideSystem), and workflow.scratchpad is for workflow contexts.

questions.question: Application developers configure ServiceNow using industry standard JavaScript to…
options: Enable the right-click to edit the context menus on applications in the navigator
Customize the organization's company logo and banner text
Configure the outgoing email display name
questions.explanation: JavaScript in ServiceNow (Client Scripts, Business Rules, Script Includes, etc.) is used to extend and add functionality to the platform. Logo customization (C), email configuration (D), and navigator menus (A) are handled through platform configuration, not JavaScript.

questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be debugged using the Field Watcher?
questions.explanation: The Field Watcher can debug Business Rules, Client Scripts, and Access Controls that are triggered by field changes. Script Includes are reusable server-side functions not directly tied to field changes, so they cannot be debugged with Field Watcher.

questions.question: Which objects can be used in Inbound Action scripts?
questions.explanation: Inbound Action scripts have access to current (the record being created/updated) and email (the incoming email details like sender, subject, body, attachments). The previous object is for Business Rules, event is deprecated in this context, and producer is for Record Producer scripts.

questions.question: To see what scripts, reports, and other application artifacts will be in a published application:
options: Enter the name of the Application in the Global search field
Open the list of Update Sets for the instance
Examine the Application Files Related List in the application to be published
Open the artifact records individually to verify the value in the Application field
questions.explanation: The Application Files Related List on the application record shows all artifacts (scripts, reports, tables, etc.) that are part of the application and will be included when published. This is the most direct and efficient way to review application contents.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a debugging strategy for client-side scripts?
questions.explanation: gs.log() is a server-side method and is NOT a client-side debugging strategy. Valid client-side debugging approaches include g_form.addInfoMessage() for visual feedback, Field Watcher for tracking field changes, jslog() for JavaScript logging, and browser developer tools.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for the Form Designer?
questions.explanation: In the Form Designer: (a) drag fields from the Fields tab to add them, (b) drag data types from Field Types tab to create new fields, and (c) hover over a field and click the Delete (X) button to remove it. (d) is false — sections are added using the section control (+), not by dragging from the Field Types tab.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for managing applications purchased from the Store?
options: There are separate entitlements for application-customizations.
Applications can be customized that belong to other organizations.
Applications can be changed that belong to other organizations.
Customizations cannot revert back to the base system application.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Store applications have separate entitlements for the base application and customizations. You cannot customize apps owned by other organizations (B, C are wrong), and customizations CAN be reverted back to the base system application (D is wrong).

questions.question: Which Script Debugger feature helps filter debugging searches to quickly narrow down script problems?
questions.explanation: The Script Tracer records script execution in real-time and provides powerful filtering capabilities to narrow down problems — filter by script name, type, error messages, or timestamps. It is the primary tool for quickly isolating script issues in the Script Debugger.

questions.question: Which API provides methods to translate text into multiple languages in real time?
questions.explanation: DynamicTranslation is the ServiceNow API designed for real-time text translation into multiple languages. The other options (DynamicResultAnswer, GeniusTranslation, GeniusResultAnswer) are not standard ServiceNow APIs.

questions.question: The getCurrentDomainID() method is part of which scoped class?
questions.explanation: ScopedSessionDomain contains the getCurrentDomainID() method, used to retrieve the current domain context in multi-domain environments. GlideSession handles session info (user ID, roles) but not domain IDs. GlideRecord is for database operations, and ScopedDCManager is not the correct class for domain context.

questions.question: _______________ is similar to ACLs in that it allows you to restrict access to certain resources, but instead of restricting tables and records from users — they restrict application resources from other applications.
questions.explanation: Application Access Settings control how other applications can access resources (scripts, UI Actions, data) within a specific application — similar to how ACLs restrict users from tables/records. Application Roles control user-level access within an app. Application Permissions is not the specific ServiceNow term for this mechanism.

questions.question: How is access to Application menus and modules controlled?
questions.explanation: Roles are the primary mechanism for controlling access to application menus and modules. Roles define which users can see and interact with specific modules. ACLs control record-level access, Application Rules automate business logic, and Client Scripts handle UI behavior — none directly control menu/module visibility.

questions.question:
A table called x is created with 3 fields: x1, x2, x3 and has the below access controls configured:
x.None read access control for users with the admin and itil role
x.* read access control for users with the admin role
x.x3 read access control for users with itil role
Which field or fields can a user with itil role read?
questions.explanation: ACL evaluation is most specific first. The x.None ACL grants record-level read to itil users. However, the field-level x.* ACL restricts all fields to admin only, blocking itil from x1 and x2. The specific x.x3 ACL grants itil access to x3. Result: an itil user can only read x3.

questions.question: g_form.getReference() function works in the Service Portal client scripts.
questions.explanation: False — g_form.getReference() is designed for the standard ServiceNow platform client scripts, not Service Portal. Service Portal uses a different scripting framework; for reference lookups there, use GlideAjax or Service Portal-specific API methods.

questions.question: Which of the following statements does NOT apply when extending an existing table?
options: The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table
You must script and configure all required behavior
The parent table's access controls are evaluated when determining access to the new table's records and fields
The new table inherits all of the fields from the parent
questions.explanation: When extending a table, the child inherits the parent's fields (D), functionality (A), and access controls (C). You do NOT need to script and configure all behavior from scratch (B) — that's the primary benefit of table extension.

questions.question: What protects applications by identifying and restricting access to application files and data?
questions.explanation: Application Scope is the primary mechanism for protecting applications by encapsulating their files and data, controlling which other applications and users can access them. ACLs control record-level access, and Roles define user permissions — but scoping provides the application-level isolation.

questions.question: All the records created using a record producer are inserted in the Requested Item (sc_req_item) table.
questions.explanation: False — Record Producers can be configured to create records in any target table, not just sc_req_item. You specify the target table when configuring the Record Producer, allowing creation of incidents, tasks, custom records, etc.

questions.question: Application files in a ServiceNow application are:
options: An XML export of the application's table records
XML exports of an application export set
CSV files containing data imported into an application
questions.explanation: Application files are the artifacts that comprise a ServiceNow application — tables, forms, scripts, workflows, UI policies, business rules, and other configuration records. They are not XML exports (A, B) or CSV data files (C).

questions.question: Schema Map is part of the Form Designer.
questions.explanation: False — The Schema Map is a separate tool that shows visual relationships between tables and fields in the database. The Form Designer is used to design and customize form layouts. They serve different purposes.

questions.question: An ACL for a table may include a table.None Access Control or a table.* Access Control but never both.
questions.explanation: False — A table can have both table.None (record-level) and table.* (all-fields) ACLs defined simultaneously. They are not mutually exclusive; ServiceNow evaluates them together to enforce layered security.

questions.question: What additional information does Debug Business Rules (Details) show in comparison to Debug Business Rules?
options: The time at which the Business Rule executed including milliseconds
Debug information from lists as well as forms
Old and new values for field values changed by the business rule
The result of the business rule's condition evaluation
questions.explanation: Debug Business Rules (Details) shows the old and new values for fields changed by the business rule. Standard Debug Business Rules shows when rules run and condition results, but the Details view adds the before/after field values — essential for understanding the exact impact of a rule.

questions.question: Client Scripts and UI Policies can execute based on view.
questions.explanation: True — Both Client Scripts and UI Policies can be configured to execute based on a specific view. You can set the 'View' field so the script/policy only runs when the form is displayed in that particular view.

questions.question: ServiceNow is good for real-time data delivery and update from external sources.
questions.explanation: False — ServiceNow is optimized for business process management and workflow automation, not real-time data streaming. It relies on scheduled imports and web service calls that may have latency. For true real-time data delivery, specialized tools like Kafka or streaming platforms are more appropriate.

questions.question: When a reference field is added to a table, does it store the number or the display value of the referenced record in the database?
options: Yes, it stores the display value of the referenced record
No, the reference field contains the sys_id of the referenced record
questions.explanation: A reference field stores the sys_id of the referenced record, not its display value or number. The sys_id is a unique 32-character identifier that ensures data integrity even if the display value changes. The display value is resolved dynamically when the field is rendered.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be debugged using the Field Watcher?
questions.explanation: Script Includes are reusable server-side functions not directly triggered by field changes. The Field Watcher can debug Business Rules, Client Scripts, and Access Controls that fire when fields change, but Script Includes are invoked programmatically and are outside Field Watcher's scope.

questions.question: Access to modules is controlled by:
questions.explanation: Roles control access to modules in the Application Navigator. ACLs handle record-level permissions, and Assignment Groups route work items — neither directly controls module visibility.

questions.question: What are embedded lists in ServiceNow?
options: Displays records in other tables that have relationships to the current record
Allows for editing related lists without having to navigate away from the form. Changes are saved when the form is saved.
questions.explanation: Embedded lists are displayed directly within the form itself, allowing users to view and edit related records without leaving the form. Changes are saved when the main form is saved. Option A describes standard related lists, which appear below the form as separate sections.

questions.question: Which of the following would NOT be a good fit for an application to run on the ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: A Virtual Reality Gaming application requires real-time 3D rendering and low-latency processing — well outside ServiceNow's strengths. ServiceNow excels at workflow automation, data management, and form-based apps, making Facilities Management (B), Billing (C), and Room Scheduling (D) all good fits.

questions.question: A UI Policy has access to a script's prior value?
questions.explanation: False — UI Policies focus on controlling field appearance based on current conditions and do not have access to the previous value of a field. In contrast, Client Scripts using the onChange event receive the old value as a parameter.

questions.question: Team Dashboard provides a central place to manage all Team Development activities on your development instance.
questions.explanation: True — The Team Dashboard centralizes all Team Development activities, providing a single view to track progress, manage code pushes/pulls, monitor conflicts, and coordinate development across instances.

questions.question: Are ACLs mandatory for privately scoped applications?
options: False, but it is a best practice
questions.explanation: ACLs are not mandatory for privately scoped applications — the platform doesn't enforce their creation. However, implementing ACLs is a security best practice to properly control data access and protect application resources.

questions.question: Script actions can be triggered using business rules apart from events?
questions.explanation: True — Script Actions are reusable server-side scripts that can be triggered by both events and business rules. Business rules can fire Script Actions when specific conditions are met (insert, update, delete), making them versatile for centralizing reusable logic.

questions.question: Script Debugger can be used to debug client-side scripts?
questions.explanation: No — The ServiceNow Script Debugger is designed for server-side scripts only (Business Rules, Script Includes). Client-side scripts run in the browser and should be debugged using the browser's built-in developer tools (Console, Sources, breakpoints).

questions.question: Removing a field from the Form Designer deletes it from the database?
questions.explanation: False — Removing a field from the Form Designer only hides it from the form view. The field and its data remain in the database. To actually delete a field from the database, you must remove it from the Dictionary.

questions.question: If there are two UI Actions with the same action name but different names, how will the system behave?
options: None of the UI Actions will execute
Both the UI Actions will execute
questions.explanation: Neither UI Action will execute. The action name is the unique identifier used to invoke a UI Action. If two UI Actions share the same action name, the system cannot resolve which one to run, resulting in a conflict where neither is triggered.

questions.question: All new tables created in ServiceNow have a default form and list layout.
questions.explanation: True — When you create a new table, ServiceNow automatically generates a default form layout (for creating/editing records) and a default list layout (for viewing records). These can be extensively customized afterward.

questions.question: Which of the below methods can be used to default the current date/time in a scoped app?
questions.explanation: In scoped applications, use new GlideDateTime().getDisplayValue() to get the current date/time in a human-readable format. gs.nowDateTime() is available in global scripts but GlideDateTime is the preferred and recommended approach in scoped apps.

questions.question: Which utility is used to determine if field names in an Import Set match the field names on the target table when importing data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Auto Map Matching Fields automatically matches Import Set field names with target table field names, reducing manual mapping effort. Transform Maps define the overall mapping but require manual configuration. Mapping Assist provides a visual interface for manual mapping.

questions.question: Is it mandatory to register an event in the Event Registry for it to be functional?
questions.explanation: Yes — Events must be explicitly registered in the Event Registry before they can trigger workflows, notifications, or Script Actions. Registration tells the platform the event exists and can be listened for.

questions.question: A new section can be added to a form using one of the field types in the Form Designer.
options: False, Sections are added by clicking the + symbol in the current section only.
questions.explanation: Sections are NOT added via field types. In the Form Designer, you add a new section by clicking the + symbol in the current section layout. Field types (string, integer, reference, etc.) are for adding data fields, not layout elements like sections.

questions.question: What is a module in ServiceNow?
options: A group of forms with a defined purpose
A separate application which is downloaded from the ServiceNow store
The functionality within an application menu such as opening a new record in the same or separate window
questions.explanation: A module is a specific functionality within an application menu — it can open a new record, display a list, navigate to a page, or run a script. It is not a group of forms (A) or a standalone downloaded application (B).

questions.question: Is it a best practice to develop applications in Global Scope?
questions.explanation: False — ServiceNow recommends developing applications in scoped (private) applications, not Global Scope. Scoped apps provide better encapsulation, security, prevent naming conflicts, and are easier to maintain and deploy across instances.

questions.question: The Form Designer can be used to design list layouts.
questions.explanation: False — The Form Designer is specifically for designing form layouts (arranging fields and sections). List layouts are managed through the List Layout Configuration tool, not the Form Designer.

questions.question: Team Development administrators can require that pushes undergo ___________ before accepting pushes.
questions.explanation: Team Development administrators can require code review before accepting pushes. This ensures code quality, adherence to standards, and reduces the risk of bugs. 'Code changes' doesn't make sense as a review prerequisite.

questions.question: When configuring a module, what does 'Override application menu roles' configuration do?
options: Admin is given access to the module even if the ACLs would prevent the access
Users with the module role but without access to the application menu can access the module
Self-service users can access the module even though they do not have roles
questions.explanation: The Override application menu roles setting allows users with the module-specific role to access the module even without the parent application menu role. It does not bypass ACLs for admins (A) or grant access to roleless users (C).

questions.question: The baseline behavior of a table in a privately scoped application is:
options: The table and its data are not accessible using web services
All application scopes can read from the table
Any business rule can read, write, update and delete from the table
Only artifacts from the table's application can read from the table
questions.explanation: By default, tables in a private scope allow read access across all application scopes. Write, update, and delete operations are restricted to the owning scope. Web services are not blocked by default (A is wrong), business rules are scoped (C is wrong), and read access is not limited to the owning app (D is wrong).

questions.question: Workflows can be used to automate UI Actions?
questions.explanation: False — Workflows automate server-side processes (task creation, approvals, notifications). UI Actions are client-side interactive elements (buttons, links) that users trigger manually. Automating UI Actions requires client-side scripting, not workflows.

questions.question: Which of the following objects does a before business rule have access to?
questions.explanation: A before business rule has access to all three: current (the record being processed), previous (the record's state before changes), and GlideRecord (the API for database operations). The current object itself is a GlideRecord instance.

questions.question: g_user.hasRole('x_foo_app_user') — does this return true for the admin role?
questions.explanation: Yes — Users with the admin role inherently have all roles in ServiceNow. g_user.hasRole('x_foo_app_user') returns true for admins because the admin role encompasses all roles on the platform.

questions.question:
An email notification can be triggered using the below options:
a) Trigger conditions
b) Events
c) Manually
questions.explanation: Email notifications can be triggered by all three methods: (a) Trigger conditions (e.g., when a field changes), (b) Events (when system events are queued), and (c) Manually (by a user or script). All three are valid, making B the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following are correct for Record Producers? (Select all that apply)
options: Record producers are used to insert and update records for a single table
Record producer forms can contain graphics and movies
Record producer variables map to table fields
UI Policies are applicable for record producers
questions.explanation: A, C, and D are correct. Record Producers target a single table (A), their variables map directly to table fields (C), and Catalog UI Policies control field behavior on Record Producer forms (D). B is incorrect — Record Producer forms use standard variables and do not support multimedia content like graphics and movies.

questions.question: The scope of a custom application can be changed at any time by a ServiceNow developer?
questions.explanation: False — Application scope is fixed at creation time and cannot be modified afterward. This immutability protects application isolation, data security, and prevents cross-scope conflicts. Developers can switch their working context using the Application Picker, but the scope of the app itself is permanent.

questions.question: While debugging security rules, what does the blue color code indicate?
options: Indicates the ACL is already in the cache and does not need to be re-evaluated
questions.explanation: In security rule debugging, blue indicates the ACL has already been evaluated and is cached — it doesn't need re-evaluation, improving performance. Green = access granted, Red = access denied.

questions.question: What module line type is used to access an Application Properties page?
questions.explanation: URL (From Arguments) directs users to a specific URL based on parameters — perfect for Application Properties pages which have their own URLs. Script executes server-side code, Single Record displays one record, and HTML renders HTML content.

questions.question: Which method is used to retrieve a system property?
questions.explanation: gs.getProperty() is the server-side method to retrieve system property values. g_form is client-side and doesn't have getProperty() or getAppProperty(). gs.getAppProperty() is not a valid ServiceNow method.

questions.question: A sequence of activities for automating processes in applications is achieved by:
questions.explanation: Workflows consist of a sequence of activities (approvals, tasks, notifications, timers) executed in a predefined order to automate business processes. UI Actions add buttons to forms (not process orchestration), and Business Rules enforce logic on individual record operations.

questions.question: An application menu can have a maximum of 10 modules.
options: False, there can be as many as required by the application
questions.explanation: False — There is no fixed limit on the number of modules in an application menu. You can add as many modules as the application design requires.

questions.question: Developers can create an _____________ to prevent pushes or pulls to particular instances in the team development hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Exclusion policies in Team Development specifically prevent pushes or pulls of certain updates to/from particular instances. Roles control user permissions but do not control the flow of updates between instances.

questions.question: The producer object is available in client scripts of a Record Producer.
questions.explanation: No — The producer object is a server-side object available in Record Producer server-side scripts (like onSubmit). Client scripts run in the browser and do not have access to the producer object.

questions.question: Any code changes done in a checked-out workflow version are applied to all ServiceNow users triggering the workflow.
questions.explanation: False — Changes to a checked-out workflow version are NOT immediately applied to all users. They only affect new workflow instances initiated after the changes are published. Existing running instances continue with the previously published version.

questions.question: Which record is generated to indicate something has occurred in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: An Event record is generated to signal that something significant occurred — it can then trigger workflows, notifications, or Script Actions. Script Actions execute scripts (not records), UI Actions add buttons, and ECC Queue handles background processing.

questions.question: What is the default scope for all custom applications that uniquely identifies them?
questions.explanation: Private scope is the default for all custom applications. It isolates the application's components (tables, scripts, etc.), prevents unintended cross-application interference, and uniquely identifies the app with a namespace like x_vendor_appname.

questions.question: What is Runtime Access Tracking for an Application?
options: Allows administrators to control access to the application settings
Allows administrators to manage script access to application resources, by creating a list of script operations and targets that the system authorizes to run — with options: None, Tracking, Enforcing
questions.explanation: Runtime Access Tracking (RAT) manages script access to application resources by maintaining a list of authorized operations. Options: None (no tracking), Tracking (logs cross-scope access), Enforcing (logs and blocks unauthorized access). It's not about general application settings (A).

questions.question: Can a scheduled job be used to run a client-side script every day?
questions.explanation: No — Scheduled Jobs execute server-side scripts only. Client-side scripts run in the user's browser and cannot be triggered by scheduled jobs. For recurring server tasks, use Scheduled Jobs; for client behavior, use Client Scripts triggered by user interaction.

questions.question: Which of the following changes are captured in Update Sets?
questions.explanation: All four are captured in Update Sets: Reports (configuration changes), CMDB schema/configuration changes (not data records), Customizations (UI policies, business rules, client scripts), and Tables & Fields (dictionary/structural changes). These are all configuration items tracked by Update Sets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method used for logging messages in a server-side script for a privately scoped application?
questions.explanation: gs.log is NOT available in privately scoped applications — it only works in Global scope. The valid scoped logging methods are: gs.warn, gs.error, gs.debug, and gs.info.

questions.question: Which is the fastest way to create and configure a Record Producer?
options: Open table in table editor and select the 'Add to Service Catalog' related link
Use the Record Producer module then add and configure the variables manually
Create a catalog category, open the category and select the 'Add new Record Producer' button
Open the table's form, right-click on form header and select the 'Create Record Producer' menu item
questions.explanation: The fastest method is to open the table and select 'Add to Service Catalog'. This directly links the Record Producer to the table and auto-populates variables based on the table's fields, significantly reducing manual configuration compared to the other methods.

questions.question: For Application Access there is a configuration called 'Allow Access to this table via web services'. Which of the following statements is true when this option is selected?
options: Even when not selected, users with correct permissions can use web services to access the table's records
The option restricts access to delete the records but allows all other access
The option restricts access only to SOAP web services and not REST API
The user performing the query via web services must have the correct permission to access the table's records
questions.explanation: Even with 'Allow Access via web services' enabled, the user must still have correct permissions (roles, ACLs) to access the data. The setting enables web service access but does not bypass security. It applies to both SOAP and REST (not just SOAP — C is wrong), and when not selected, web service access is blocked regardless of permissions (A is wrong).

questions.question: A ServiceNow developer can push updates to any server in the Team Development hierarchy?
questions.explanation: False — In Team Development, each instance has exactly one designated Parent instance. Developers can only push changes to that parent, not to any arbitrary server in the hierarchy. This ensures a controlled flow of code with proper conflict resolution.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements must evaluate to true to grant a user access to an application table's record?
a) Conditions configured in the access controls must evaluate to true
b) Scripts configured in the access control must evaluate to true
c) The user has one of the roles specified in the required roles related list
d) Other matching access controls for the records evaluate to true
questions.explanation: For a single ACL to pass, all three must be true: (a) conditions, (b) scripts, and (c) roles. Statement (d) is false because multiple matching ACLs are evaluated with an OR condition — only one ACL needs to pass, not all of them.

questions.question: A custom application 'XYZ' has table 'XYTable' with Application Access: Accessible from All Application Scopes, Can read: Selected, Can delete: Selected, Allow configuration: Selected. Which of the following is true?
options: No script can be written outside the application which can successfully delete records in table XYTable
An application developer working in another privately scoped app can write a business rule which successfully deletes all records from the XYTable
questions.explanation: With Accessible from: All Application Scopes and Can delete: Selected, other applications are explicitly granted delete access. A developer in another scoped app can write a business rule that deletes records from XYTable. Option A is wrong because cross-scope delete access has been explicitly enabled.

questions.question: When creating application tables, a user role is automatically added to the table record. Which other role does an application typically have?
questions.explanation: When creating an application, ServiceNow automatically creates a user role and an admin role for the application. The admin role grants comprehensive access to configure the application, manage data, and control access. The other options are not standard auto-generated roles.

questions.question: Which is the correct link type to use when creating a module which opens a Record Producer?
questions.explanation: URL (from arguments) is used to navigate to a specific URL within ServiceNow, including Record Producer forms. You can pass form arguments to pre-populate fields. Script executes server-side code (A), HTML renders content (B), and Content Page displays static content (C).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the gs.isInteractive() function in Business Rules?
options: The function returns true if the action is performed by an interactive user
The function returns true when an event is triggered
The function returns true when a UI Action is clicked
questions.explanation: gs.isInteractive() returns true when the action is performed by an interactive user (someone using the browser). It returns false for automated processes like scheduled jobs, web service calls, or data imports. This lets you conditionally execute logic only for user-initiated actions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a UI Action type?
questions.explanation: Form choice is NOT a valid UI Action type. The standard types include: Form button, Form link, Form context menu, List choice, List banner button, and List bottom button.

questions.question: Which of the below is the best practice for adding instructions to a form?
questions.explanation: Annotations are the best practice for adding instructions to a form. They provide clean, context-sensitive help text directly on the form without cluttering the UI. Read-only fields add clutter (A), wiki links navigate away (C), and context menus are less visible (D).

questions.question: Developers DO/DO NOT create application file records directly from the Application File table.
questions.explanation: Developers DO NOT create application file records directly in the sys_app_file table. Application files are created indirectly through Studio, by creating configuration records (tables, scripts, forms), or by importing update sets. The system manages file records automatically.

questions.question: If there is a role 'pa_admin', which method should be used to exclusively check if a user has the specified role?
questions.explanation: g_user.hasRoleExactly() checks if the user has the exact specified role, without considering inherited roles. hasRole() would also return true for admin users (who inherit all roles). hasRoleOnly() and hasRoleFromList() are not valid ServiceNow methods.

questions.question: What are the Client Script types?
questions.explanation: The four Client Script types are: onLoad (when form loads), onChange (when a field value changes), onSubmit (before form submission), and onCellEdit (when editing in a list view). Option B describes Business Rule types, and C is incomplete.

questions.question: By default, are new table records available for viewing by users?
options: No, a user will not be able to see the table records unless they satisfy the ACLs on the table
questions.explanation: No — Users cannot view records unless they satisfy the ACLs (Access Control Lists) on the table. ACLs enforce role-based and condition-based access, so users must meet the defined criteria to read, write, create, or delete records.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true about client-side scripted security?
options: Client-side scripts have access to the GlideUser (g_user) methods
Client-side scripts have access to the GlideSystem (gs) user methods
Client-side scripts have no access to the GlideSystem (gs) user methods
Client-side scripts have access to both GlideSystem (gs) and GlideUser (g_user) methods
questions.explanation: Client-side scripts have access to g_user for user properties and methods like hasRole(). gs (GlideSystem) is server-side only and is not available in client scripts. So B and D are wrong, and C incorrectly denies g_user access.

questions.question: Who sets the glide.appcreator.company.code property?
questions.explanation: The glide.appcreator.company.code property is set by ServiceNow automatically. It defines a unique company code used in application scope namespaces and is not intended to be manually modified by administrators.

questions.question: In a Business Rule, which of the following returns the sys_id of the currently logged-in user?
questions.explanation: gs.getUserID() returns the sys_id of the currently logged-in user on the server side. g_form is client-side only (A, C are invalid in Business Rules). gs.getUserSysID() is not a valid method (B is wrong).

questions.question: How do you get to the mobile version of ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Append $m.do to the ServiceNow instance URL to access the mobile interface. $mobile.do and $mobnav.do are not valid URL suffixes.

questions.question: current.isNew() is a valid function which returns true if the record being created is a new record.
options: False, current.isNewRecord() is the correct function which returns true for a new record
questions.explanation: current.isNew() is NOT a valid ServiceNow method. The correct method is current.isNewRecord(), which returns true if the record has not yet been saved to the database.

questions.question: What checkbox is selected in ACL configuration to display the Script field?
questions.explanation: Selecting the Advanced checkbox in the ACL configuration reveals the Script field, enabling you to write custom scripts for the access control rule. There is no separate 'Script' checkbox.

questions.question: What ways can a form field be made read-only?
questions.explanation: Fields can be made read-only via: Field Attributes (dictionary 'Read only' checkbox), Client Scripts (g_form.setReadOnly()), and UI Policies (no-code recommended approach). UI Actions (A) add buttons, not field states. Business Rules (E) are server-side and cannot directly set form field appearance.

questions.question: When you move code changes to a private application scope, you must add the scope namespace qualifier to each function call.
questions.explanation: True — Private scopes create a unique namespace (e.g., x_vendor_app). When moving code into a scoped app, function calls must include the scope namespace qualifier so the system correctly resolves references within that scope.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow App Store?
options: A store for purchasing ServiceNow plugins
A forum where you can discuss ServiceNow issues
A website for downloading ServiceNow applications
A portal where incidents can be logged for HI Support
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow App Store is the official marketplace for browsing, downloading, and installing ServiceNow applications and integrations. It's not limited to plugins (A), it's not a forum (B), and HI Support is a separate portal (D).

questions.question: In a Transform Map, only one field can be used for coalesce?
questions.explanation: False — Transform Maps support multiple coalesce fields. Multiple fields can be marked for coalescing, allowing records to be uniquely identified by a combination of field values during import.

questions.question: Can you copy a custom application from one instance to another?
questions.explanation: Yes — Custom applications can be copied between instances using update sets, the Application Repository, or ServiceNow Studio's source control integration.

questions.question: Update Sets track customizations where the table has an 'update_synch' dictionary attribute.
questions.explanation: True — Tables with the update_synch=true dictionary attribute have their record changes automatically tracked in the current Update Set (via the sys_update_xml table). Most configuration tables have this attribute out-of-the-box.

questions.question: Records are created in the Application Cross-Scope Access table when the Runtime Access Tracking Setting is set to:
questions.explanation: Records are created when set to Tracking (logs access attempts) or Enforcing (logs and blocks unauthorized access). When set to None, no cross-scope access records are created.

questions.question: ServiceNow recommends creating all new applications in this type of application scope:
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends Private Scope for all new applications. It provides isolation, encapsulation, prevents naming conflicts, and ensures better security, versioning, and deployment practices compared to Global scope.

questions.question: The protection policy on a Script Include is useful to protect code for applications published to the ServiceNow Store?
questions.explanation: Yes — The protection policy on a Script Include prevents others from viewing or modifying the code, safeguarding intellectual property for applications published to the ServiceNow Store.

questions.question: Can a field's database name be changed once it has been created?
questions.explanation: No — Once a field's database name (column name) is created, it cannot be changed. Modifying it would break data integrity, references, scripts, and the database schema. You can change the field's label, but not its database name.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true for Scripted REST API?
a) They are faster compared to standard table REST API
b) They can be used to combine data from multiple tables
c) They are used to limit access to system tables
d) They are useful when a REST operation involves complex operations
questions.explanation: (b) and (d) are true. Scripted REST APIs can combine data from multiple tables (b) and handle complex operations beyond basic CRUD (d). They are NOT necessarily faster (a — depends on script complexity), and access control is managed by ACLs, not Scripted REST APIs (c).

questions.question: Applications can access and change their own tables and business logic, but other applications (such as Incident Management) cannot make changes to them without explicit permission.
questions.explanation: True — Each scoped application owns its resources and has full CRUD access to its own tables and scripts. Out-of-scope applications are restricted by default and require explicit cross-scope privileges (via Application Access settings) to modify another application's data.

questions.question: The Field Watcher can be used to debug multiple fields at the same time?
questions.explanation: False — The Field Watcher can only watch one field at a time. To observe another field, you must stop watching the current one and start a new session for the other field.

questions.question: More than one update set can be the default set for any application scope.
questions.explanation: False — Only one update set can be the default for any application scope at a time. Setting a new default automatically deselects the previous one, ensuring changes are tracked consistently.

questions.question: Application properties can have a reference field as their data type.
questions.explanation: False — Application properties support basic data types (strings, integers, booleans, dates) but do not support complex types like reference fields. Reference fields link to other table records and are not applicable for simple configuration properties.

questions.question: An application owns its tables and determines whether other applications can access resources from them.
questions.explanation: True — Each scoped application owns its tables and controls cross-scope access through Application Access settings. Other applications must be granted explicit permission to read, create, update, or delete records.

questions.question: Which objects can be used in Inbound Action scripts?
questions.explanation: Inbound Action scripts have access to: current (record being processed), email (inbound email details — sender, subject, body), and event (the triggering event). producer is for Record Producer scripts, and previous is for Business Rules.

questions.question: ServiceNow is good for media streaming.
questions.explanation: False — ServiceNow is designed for IT service management, workflow automation, and business process management. It is not optimized for media streaming, which requires specialized real-time content delivery infrastructure.

questions.question: When a ServiceNow instance requests information from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service:
questions.explanation: When ServiceNow requests data from an external web service, it acts as the Consumer. The external system serving the data is the Provider. Publisher and Broadcaster are not standard web service roles.

questions.question: What are the 2 core tables from which all other tables are extended in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The two core foundation tables are task (parent of incident, problem, change_request, etc.) and cmdb_ci (parent of all Configuration Items). incident is a child of task (A is wrong), and cmdb is a container, not the CI foundation table (B is wrong).

questions.question: Team Development uses Git to manage versions.
questions.explanation: False — Team Development does NOT use Git. It uses version records stored within the platform to track changes, detect conflicts, enable branching, and merge code. Git is a separate external version control system used with Studio source control.

questions.question: What is the option in Table configuration that allows a table to be extended?
questions.explanation: The Extensible field on the table record determines whether other tables can extend (inherit from) this table. 'Can be Extended' is not the exact ServiceNow label (A), and 'Extended By' shows which tables already extend it (C).

questions.question: What are the 3 basic components of a Workflow?
questions.explanation: The three basic workflow components are Approvals (authorization steps), Notifications (informing stakeholders), and Tasks (work items). Scripts (B) add custom logic but are not a core component. Timers (C) control timing but are not one of the three basics.

questions.question: Can an application have more than one default update set?
questions.explanation: No — Only one update set can be the default for an application scope at a time. When you set one as default, the system automatically removes the default status from all others in that scope.

questions.question: While accessing a table using REST API, is authentication required for every request sent to the server?
questions.explanation: Yes — REST APIs are stateless. Every request must include valid authentication credentials (Basic Auth, OAuth token, etc.) to ensure the requester is authorized. There is no persistent session across requests.

questions.question: A Display Business Rule does NOT have access to the following object:
questions.explanation: Display Business Rules run before a record is loaded to the form. The previous object (prior values before an update) is NOT available at this stage. They DO have access to current, GlideSystem (gs), and g_scratchpad — populating g_scratchpad is the primary purpose of Display rules.

questions.question: Which of the following functions is NOT available in the ServiceNow REST API?
questions.explanation: COPY is not a standard HTTP method and is not available in the ServiceNow REST API. The supported methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.

questions.question: In an Email Notification, which of the following is NOT true for the Weight field?
options: A weight value of zero means no email should be sent
Only notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipient are sent
The weight value defaults to zero
questions.explanation: A weight of zero does NOT mean no email is sent — it means the notification always sends when criteria are met. Non-zero weighted notifications compete, with only the highest weight winning (B is true). The default weight is zero (C is true).

questions.question: Can token-based/OAuth authentication be used in ServiceNow when consuming REST API?
questions.explanation: Yes — ServiceNow supports OAuth and token-based authentication for consuming REST APIs. This allows secure authorization through token exchanges instead of sending credentials with every request.

questions.question: Which features are available for both Scoped and Global Applications? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: Develop in Studio (A) and Flow Designer (B) are available for both scoped and global apps. Source Control (C) is primarily a scoped application feature.

questions.question: Delegated Development is available for:
questions.explanation: Delegated Development is available for scoped applications only. It allows administrators to grant non-admin users the ability to develop within a specific scoped application. It does not extend to global applications.

questions.question: What is NOT possible in Flow Designer?
options: Run a flow from Service Catalog
questions.explanation: Flow Designer does NOT support 'Run As' testing — that feature exists in the legacy Workflow Editor. Flow Designer does support Service Catalog triggers (A), subflows (C), and stages (D).

questions.question: What is a new option when creating a custom application using Studio?
questions.explanation: Start from global is a creation option in Studio that allows developers to build applications leveraging the global scope. Studio does not offer 'Copy from existing application' (B) or 'Start from existing service' (C) as standard creation options.

questions.question: Dashboard sharing notifications are customizable.
questions.explanation: True — Dashboard sharing notifications can be customized, including the content, recipients, and branding, to align with organizational communication needs.

questions.question: Is it possible to rollback both Global and Scoped Applications?
questions.explanation: Yes — Both Global and Scoped applications support rollback. You can revert changes using update sets or version control mechanisms to restore a previous state.

questions.question: What is NOT applicable for extension points?
options: By altering the base code of an application using extension points, it's easier to integrate customizations
Application customizers use extension points to add functionality to the base application
Application creators can place hooks, called extension points, in scoped and global application base code
questions.explanation: Option A is NOT applicable — extension points are specifically designed to avoid altering base code. They provide hooks for customizers to extend functionality without modifying the original application, preventing upgrade conflicts. B and C are correct descriptions of extension points.

questions.question: Can you select the format (Multipart, Binary, Text) of a REST message when writing a REST step using Flow Designer?
questions.explanation: Yes — In Flow Designer's REST step, you can select the message format (Multipart, Binary, or Text) to match the requirements of the external service you're integrating with.

questions.question: In relation to application files, which of the below is False?
options: Move existing globally scoped metadata files between global applications
Remove files from the currently selected global application
Move files in and out of a scoped application
questions.explanation: Moving files in and out of a scoped application is False. Scoped applications enforce strict isolation — files cannot be transferred across scope boundaries. You CAN move global metadata between global apps (A) and remove files from a global app (B).

questions.question: On which type of custom table can I use Mobile Studio?
options: On all custom tables under the App Engine License with 'Pro' subscription or higher, and custom tables assigned to 'Pro' bundle subscriptions or higher
On all custom tables under App Engine License with 'Pro' subscription, Grandfather subscription tables, and all product bundle tables
On all custom tables for which the Mobile Studio license Add-On is purchased
On all tables under Now Platform App Engine subscription and product bundle tables, but not Grandfathered tables
On all tables regardless of subscription for post-Madrid; for pre-Madrid only on OOB applications
questions.explanation: Mobile Studio is available on custom tables under the App Engine License with 'Pro' subscription or higher and custom tables assigned to 'Pro' bundle subscriptions or higher. Grandfathered subscriptions are no longer supported (B wrong), there's no separate add-on (C wrong), and it's not universally available (E wrong).

questions.question: How does ServiceNow determine if a user has the right to use a custom table under the Now Platform App Engine Subscription?
options: ServiceNow checks which users accessed which tables during compliance period and verifies against license subscription
A user that has been provided rights to create, read, update, or delete on a custom table is considered a User of that table regardless of actual usage
Users are subscribed to an application to access it; all tables within scope are designated accessible
Operator license users access all tables in scope; Requester type only accesses the primary table
questions.explanation: ServiceNow determines table usage by permissions granted, not actual usage. Any user with CRUD rights on a custom table is counted as a User of that table for licensing purposes, regardless of whether they actually access it.
