Why others are wrong: A) Display BRs DO have access to g_scratchpad for passing data from server to client. C) Display BRs DO have access to current (the record being displayed). D) Display BRs DO have access to gs (GlideSystem) for system methods.

questions.question: How do you access the mobile version of ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: To access the mobile version of ServiceNow, navigate to your_instance.service-now.com/$m.do. The $m.do URL redirects to the mobile-optimized interface. Why others are wrong: A) $mobnav.do is not a valid ServiceNow URL. B) $mobile.do is not a valid ServiceNow URL. The correct short form is $m.do.

questions.question: Which objects can be used in Inbound Action scripts?
questions.explanation: Inbound Action scripts use the current object (to set field values on the record being created/updated) and the email object (to access email properties like body_text, subject, sender). Example: current.short_description = email.subject;. Why others are wrong: B) 'producer' is not an available object in Inbound Actions. C) 'event' is not available — the email object handles the inbound data. D) 'previous' is for update business rules, not Inbound Actions.

questions.question: Which of the following is True for GlideUser methods?
options: It can be used in client scripts and UI Policies only
It can be used in business rules only
It can be used in Client scripts, UI Policies and UI actions only
It can be used in business rules and script includes
questions.explanation: GlideUser methods (g_user) are client-side and available in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions. They provide information about the currently logged-in user for controlling UI behavior. Why others are wrong: A) Too restrictive — GlideUser is also available in UI Actions. B) Business rules use server-side APIs (gs, current, previous), not g_user. D) Script includes are server-side and don't have access to g_user.

questions.question: How do you automatically populate the assigned_to field on an incident task as soon as it is created?
options: Add a data policy on incident task
Use Flow Designer based approach with no scripting. Save and activate the flow
Use a before insert Business Rule to set default assigned_to values
Define UI Policy to set assigned_to value
questions.explanation: Flow Designer can automatically set the assigned_to field when an incident task is created — a modern, no-code approach aligned with best practices. Before insert Business Rule can also populate assigned_to at record creation — a traditional scripting approach. Why others are wrong: A) Data policies enforce field requirements but don't auto-populate values. D/E) UI Policies only affect the form display for users — they can't populate values automatically at server-side record creation.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a purpose of application scoping?
options: Provide a custom way of solving specific business problems
Provide controls for how scripts from another scope can alter tables in a scoped application
Provide a way of tracking users who developed the application
Provide a relationship between application artifacts
questions.explanation: Tracking users who developed the application is NOT a purpose of application scoping. Scoping focuses on isolation, security, and organization — not developer tracking (which is handled by Change Management and version control). Why others are wrong: A) Scoping DOES provide custom solutions by isolating customizations. B) Scoping DOES control cross-scope script interactions. D) Scoping DOES provide relationships between application artifacts.

questions.question: In a business rule, which of the following returns the sys_id of the currently logged-in user?
questions.explanation: In a business rule (server-side), gs.getUserID() is the correct method. Business rules use gs (GlideSystem) for server-side methods, and getUserID() returns the sys_id of the current user session. Why others are wrong: A) g_form is a client-side object — not available in business rules. C) gs.getuserSysID() is not a valid GlideSystem method — using it would cause an error.

questions.question: What are the 3 most common extended tables off CMDB?
questions.explanation: Neither A nor B — both options list tables that are NOT part of the CMDB. The 3 most common extended CMDB tables are: cmdb_ci (primary CI table), cmdb_ci_computer (physical/virtual computers), and cmdb_ci_network (network devices like routers/switches). Why others are wrong: A) sys_user, sys_user_group, kb_knowledge are user, group, and knowledge tables — none are CMDB tables. B) Same issue — sys_user, sys_group, sys_knowledge are not CMDB tables.

questions.question: What is the difference between Audit sets and History sets?
options: The History Set [sys_history_set] table stores historical information forever for all records
The Audit [sys_audit] table identifies records with history; History [sys_history_line] stores actual changes
The Audit [sys_audit] table stores historical information forever for all records
The History Set [sys_history_set] table identifies records with history; History [sys_history_line] stores actual field-level changes
questions.explanation: History Set (sys_history_set) acts as a pointer identifying which records have historical data, containing metadata like record ID and table name. History Line (sys_history_line) stores the actual field-level changes (old/new values). The Audit table (sys_audit) is a legacy table deprecated in favor of this split approach. Why others are wrong: A) sys_history_set doesn't store changes — it only references records. B) sys_audit is deprecated in modern versions. C) sys_audit is legacy and doesn't store data 'forever.'

questions.question: Which API provides methods to translate text into multiple languages in real time?
questions.explanation: DynamicTranslation is the dedicated ServiceNow API for real-time text translation. It leverages translation services (Microsoft Azure Translator, Google Cloud Translation) to translate text and detect languages. Why others are wrong: B) GeniusTranslation is not a standard ServiceNow API. C) DynamicResultAnswer is related to Virtual Agent response processing, not text translation.

questions.question: The getCurrentDomainID() method is part of which scoped class?
questions.explanation: ScopedSessionDomain contains the getCurrentDomainID() method. This class provides domain-related methods within scoped applications for retrieving the current domain context in multi-domain environments. Why others are wrong: A) ScopedDomain sounds similar but is not the correct class. C) GlideRecord is for database operations. D) GlideSession manages session info but not domain ID retrieval. E) ScopedDCManager is not related to domain ID retrieval.

questions.question: You can use AI Search Assist to achieve which of the following?
options: Create a search profile that can link to a portal
Add Knowledge Base articles or Catalog items
questions.explanation: AI Search Assist is used to add Knowledge Base articles or Catalog Items as suggestions to users as they type. It helps deflect cases by guiding users to existing information before they submit a new request. Why others are wrong: A) Creating REST API endpoints is done through other platform tools, not AI Search Assist. B) While AI Search Assist relies on search profiles, you don't use AI Search Assist itself to create them — that's configured in the AI Search module separately.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for managing applications purchased from the Store?
options: There are separate entitlements for application customizations
Customizations cannot revert back to the base system application
Applications can be customized that belong to other organizations
questions.explanation: Customizations cannot revert back to the base system application. When you customize a Store-purchased app, those changes are layered on top of the baseline. There's no one-click rollback — you must manually undo customizations to restore the original version. Why others are wrong: A) Entitlements apply to the application itself, not separately to customizations. C) You cannot customize applications belonging to other organizations — customizations are limited to apps in your own instance.
